title: Electrical characteristics of servos and introduction to the servo control interface
creator: Pololu
prerequisites: Motor, transmission, and feedback distinctions from Chapter 2.
why: Separates supply energy from the low-power command signal and explains its reference.
first_task: Identify power, ground, and signal in a selected servo manual; record the permitted supply and signal levels.
limitations: RC examples do not establish wiring requirements for isolated drives or serial-bus products.
evidence_note: Opened the official article; power leads, pulse command, and ground reference are described.

title: Servo control interface in detail
creator: Pololu
prerequisites: Motor, transmission, and feedback distinctions from Chapter 2.
why: Explains pulse-width mapping, calibration, and analog-versus-digital internal servo behavior.
first_task: Explain why a library command labelled 90 degrees needs a calibrated pulse-to-angle mapping.
limitations: Timing examples are illustrative; read the actual servo limits before commanding its endpoints.
evidence_note: Opened official article; inspected pulse width, period, and digital servo discussion.

title: Continuous Rotation Servos
creator: Pololu
prerequisites: Motor, transmission, and feedback distinctions from Chapter 2.
why: Shows why a continuous-rotation label does not promise angle positioning.
first_task: Compare an ordinary continuous-rotation unit with a feedback-equipped example; identify which loop the host must add.
limitations: Manufacturer catalog examples; no listed servo has been selected or tested for this guide.
evidence_note: Opened official category explanation and comparison with the feedback column.

title: Servo System Overview
creator: Kollmorgen
prerequisites: Motor, transmission, and feedback distinctions from Chapter 2.
why: Connects the industrial motor, feedback unit, amplifier, load, and control loops.
first_task: Sketch which purchased components are needed in addition to a bare servo motor.
limitations: Drive-specific documentation; compatibility and installation requirements must come from the chosen system.
evidence_note: Opened official overview; inspected component roles, feedback, and control-loop explanation.

title: AXIS_SERVO_DRIVE Diagrams
creator: Rockwell Automation
prerequisites: Motor, transmission, and feedback distinctions from Chapter 2.
why: Contrasts motor-side, load-side, and dual position feedback configurations.
first_task: Locate the sensor used for position in each arrangement and explain what gearbox deformation a motor encoder misses.
limitations: Specific control architectures; adding an output sensor still requires a compatible drive and appropriate tuning.
evidence_note: Opened official documentation; inspected Motor Position, Auxiliary Position, and Dual Position descriptions.

title: AK80-9 V3.0 Robotic Actuator
creator: CubeMars
prerequisites: Motor, transmission, and feedback distinctions from Chapter 2.
why: Provides a current example of a motor, planetary reducer, encoder, and drive integrated into one joint module.
first_task: List what is included, then find the output-load and cooling details that a complete mechanism still needs.
limitations: Example package only; product claims and peak ratings do not rate our printed pivot. No purchase recommendation.
evidence_note: Opened official product page; integration, supported control modes, and single-encoder listing are present.

title: What is a Frameless Motor?
creator: Kollmorgen
prerequisites: Motor, transmission, and feedback distinctions from Chapter 2.
why: Distinguishes a rotor/stator motor kit from a housed motor or complete robot joint.
first_task: List the bearing, housing, alignment, thermal, and feedback jobs transferred to the mechanism designer.
limitations: Manufacturer overview; installation tolerances and thermal ratings need the selected motor documentation.
evidence_note: Opened official explanation; inspected kit contents and integration responsibilities.
